key_insight: Nb and Ta preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B₂, linking favorable boundary bonding and lower boundary energies to stronger interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary chemistry could improve the mechanical performance of high-entropy diboride ceramics.
method: DFT calculations of four grain-boundary types in five binary diborides and HEB₂.
COHP analysis of metal–boron bonding near the Fermi level.
Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics segregation sampling at six HEB₂ boundaries using a fine-tuned MACE potential.
evidence_signal: Nb and Ta were enriched at five of six simulated boundaries, reaching 23–35 at.% at 2000 K; a segregated Σ193 boundary sustained 26 GPa versus 20 GPa for a random boundary in tension at 300 K.
watch_item: The computational findings require experimental validation, and the reported tensile-strength gain is specific to the tested Σ193 boundary.
paper_title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties
